_meta.indication: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group I) to delay disease progression and reduce the risk of hospitalization for PAH

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven study with dose titration and maintenance phases
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with symptomatic pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group I), predominantly WHO Functional Class II (46%) and III (53%); idiopathic/heritable PAH (58%), connective tissue disease (29%), congenital heart disease with repaired shunts (10%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to first morbidity/mortality event up to end-of-treatment (death, hospitalization for PAH, PAH worsening requiring lung transplantation or balloon atrial septostomy, initiation of parenteral prostanoid/chronic oxygen therapy, or other disease progression [15% decrease in 6MWD plus worsening functional class or need for other therapy])
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint events occurred in 27.0% (155/574) of UPTRAVI vs 41.6% (242/582) of placebo patients; Hazard Ratio 0.60 (99% CI 0.46, 0.78), p-value <0.0001 — a 40% reduction in the risk of morbidity/mortality events

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% more than placebo) were headache (65% vs 32%), diarrhea (42% vs 18%), jaw pain (26% vs 6%), nausea (33% vs 18%), myalgia (16% vs 6%), vomiting (18% vs 9%), pain in extremity (17% vs 8%), and flushing (12% vs 5%) — typical prostacyclin-associated effects.
target_moa: Selexipag is an oral, selective prostacyclin receptor (IP receptor) agonist, structurally distinct from prostacyclin; it is hydrolyzed by carboxylesterase 1 to an active metabolite ~37-fold more potent. IP receptor stimulation leads to vasodilatory, anti-proliferative, and anti-fibrotic effects.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA Advisory Committee because the drug is not the first in its class and its safety profile is similar to other approved drugs for this indication.
